Source code for test.test_sync_com_manager

   1"""Unit tests for the sync_com_manager module.
   2
   3This module contains comprehensive unit tests for the synchronous, thread-based MQTT
   4communication management classes defined in step_lib.sync_com_manager, including:
   5
   6    - ConnectionStatus: Connection status enumeration
   7    - SyncComManager.Command: Base class for internal queue commands
   8    - SyncComManager.ExitThreadsCommand: Command used to terminate background threads
   9    - SyncComManager.SubscribeCommand: Command used to request a topic subscription
  10    - SyncComManager: Thread-based synchronous MQTT communication manager
  11
  12``SyncComManagerParams`` (defined in the separate step_lib.sync_com_manager_params
  13module, to avoid an import cycle) has its own dedicated test module,
  14test_sync_com_manager_params.py; it is used here only as configuration input via the
  15``sync_com_manager_params`` fixture.
  16
  17Test coverage includes initialization, attribute assignment, slot definitions, the
  18context-manager protocol, start/stop lifecycle handling, subscribe/publish dispatch,
  19the background thread's command loop and reconnection logic, and correct delegation to
  20the underlying AsyncComManager collaborator (mocked throughout, with three deliberate
  21exceptions: test_stop_during_reconnect_does_not_hang_or_raise_unexpectedly,
  22test_restart_after_stop, and
  23test_publish_its_message_does_not_block_and_raises_when_queue_full each run a real
  24background Thread and a real asyncio event loop, since the behavior they guard against
  25can only be observed with genuine cross-thread timing rather than a mocked loop/thread).
  26
  27Complexity:
  28    - Time: O(1) for most tests, which perform a fixed, constant number of mocked calls
  29      or assertions; O(n) for test_message_receive_thread and its nested
  30      async_message_generator, where n is message_count, and for
  31      test_subscribe_command_exec, where n is the length of topics.
  32    - Space: O(1) for most tests, holding only a fixed number of local references; O(n)
  33      for the tests listed above, proportional to message_count or len(topics).
  34"""
  35

 282    def test_init(
 283        self, sync_com_manager_params: SyncComManagerParams, manager: SyncComManager
 284    ) -> None:
 285        """Test the initialization of the SyncComManager class.
 286
 287        Ensures that the manager stores the given params, creates correctly sized
 288        queues, creates a non-started daemon background thread, and starts in the
 289        DISCONNECTED state.
 290
 291        Args:
 292            sync_com_manager_params (SyncComManagerParams): The parameters used to
 293                construct the manager.
 294            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 295
 296        Returns:
 297            None
 298        """
 299        # Arrange & Act done via fixtures
 300        # Assert
 301        assert manager._params == sync_com_manager_params
 302        # The incoming command queue is created per event loop by _run, not here
 303        assert manager._incoming_queue is None
 304        assert (
 305            manager._outgoing_queue.maxsize
 306            == sync_com_manager_params.max_outgoing_queue_rooms
 307        )
 308        assert manager._async_thread.name == "async_thread"
 309        assert manager._async_thread.daemon is True
 310        assert manager._async_thread.is_alive() is False
 311        assert manager._async_loop is None
 312        assert manager._subscribe_topics is None
 313        assert manager._async_threads == []
 314        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STOPPED
 315        assert manager.connection_status == ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED
 316        assert isinstance(manager._worker_pool, PublishWorkerPool)
 317        assert manager._worker_pool.is_running is False
 318        assert manager._health_check_thread.name == "publish_health_check_thread"
 319        assert manager._health_check_thread.daemon is True
 320        assert manager._health_check_thread.is_alive() is False
 321        assert manager._health_check_stop_event.is_set() is False

 323    def test_enter(self, mocker: MockerFixture, manager: SyncComManager) -> None:
 324        """Test that __enter__ starts the manager and returns self.
 325
 326        Args:
 327            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch start().
 328            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 329
 330        Returns:
 331            None
 332        """
 333        # Arrange
 334        # SyncComManager defines __slots__, so instance-level attribute patching is
 335        # not possible; the method is patched on the class instead. Because a plain
 336        # Mock does not implement the descriptor protocol, it is not bound to the
 337        # instance, so the recorded call carries no "self" argument.
 338        mock_start = mocker.patch.object(SyncComManager, "start")
 339        # Act
 340        result = manager.__enter__()
 341        # Assert
 342        mock_start.assert_called_once_with()
 343        assert result is manager

 400    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
 401        argnames=("queue_maxsize", "message_count", "expected_queued_count"),
 402        argvalues=[(10, 2, 2), (1, 2, 1)],
 403    )
 404    @pytest.mark.parametrize(argnames="logging_enabled", argvalues=[True, False])
 405    @pytest.mark.asyncio
 406    async def test_message_receive_thread(
 407        self,
 408        *,
 409        mocker: MockerFixture,
 410        mock_logger: MagicMock,
 411        manager: SyncComManager,
 412        queue_maxsize: int,
 413        message_count: int,
 414        expected_queued_count: int,
 415        logging_enabled: bool,
 416    ) -> None:
 417        """Test that _message_receive_thread enqueues received message payloads and
 418        drops (with a warning) any message that does not fit in a full outgoing
 419        queue, logging only when the relevant level is enabled.
 420
 421        Args:
 422            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to build mock
 423                messages.
 424            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
 425            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 426            queue_maxsize (int): The maxsize of the outgoing queue to test with.
 427            message_count (int): The number of incoming messages to simulate.
 428            expected_queued_count (int): The number of messages expected to have been
 429                successfully queued.
 430            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports every level as
 431                enabled.
 432
 433        Returns:
 434            None
 435        """
 436        # Arrange
 437        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
 438        manager._outgoing_queue = SyncQueue(maxsize=queue_maxsize)
 439        payloads = [
 440            mocker.MagicMock(spec=FacilityMessage) for _ in range(message_count)
 441        ]
 442        its_messages = [
 443            mocker.MagicMock(qos=1, topic=f"topic_{i}", its_payload=payloads[i])
 444            for i in range(message_count)
 445        ]
 446
 447        async def async_message_generator() -> AsyncGenerator[MagicMock, None]:
 448            """Yield the simulated ITS messages one at a time.
 449
 450            Yields:
 451                MagicMock: The next simulated ITS message.
 452
 453            Returns:
 454                None
 455
 456            Complexity:
 457                - Time: O(n), where n is the length of its_messages, to yield every
 458                  message.
 459                - Space: O(1), only the loop variable is held; its_messages already
 460                  exists in the enclosing scope.
 461            """
 462            for msg in its_messages:
 463                yield msg
 464
 465        client = mocker.MagicMock()
 466        client.its_messages = async_message_generator()
 467        # Act
 468        await manager._message_receive_thread(client=client)
 469        # Assert
 470        queued = []
 471        while not manager._outgoing_queue.empty():
 472            queued.append(manager._outgoing_queue.get_nowait())
 473        assert queued == payloads[:expected_queued_count]
 474        if expected_queued_count < message_count and logging_enabled:
 475            mock_logger.warning.assert_called()
 476        else:
 477            mock_logger.warning.assert_not_called()
 478        if logging_enabled:
 479            mock_logger.info.assert_called()
 480        else:
 481            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()


 482

 539        topics: list[str] | None,
 540        expect_unsubscribe_call: bool,
 541        logging_enabled: bool,
 542    ) -> None:
 543        """Test that _unsubscribe_topics unsubscribes from any previously subscribed,
 544        non-empty topic list, always clears _subscribe_topics afterward, and only
 545        logs when the relevant level is enabled.
 546
 547        Args:
 548            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to build the mock
 549                client.
 550            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
 551            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 552            topics (list[str] | None): The previously subscribed topics, or None
 553                if there were none.
 554            expect_unsubscribe_call (bool): Whether client.unsubscribe is expected to
 555                be awaited.
 556            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports every level as
 557                enabled.
 558
 559        Returns:
 560            None
 561        """
 562        # Arrange
 563        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
 564        client = mocker.MagicMock()
 565        client.unsubscribe = mocker.AsyncMock()
 566        if topics is None:
 567            manager._subscribe_topics = None
 568        else:
 569            manager._subscribe_topics = SyncComManager.SubscribeCommand(
 570                topics=topics, max_qos=MqttQoS.QOS_1
 571            )
 572        # Act
 573        await manager._unsubscribe_topics(client=client)
 574        # Assert
 575        if expect_unsubscribe_call:
 576            client.unsubscribe.assert_awaited_once_with(topic=topics)
 577        else:
 578            client.unsubscribe.assert_not_awaited()
 579        assert manager._subscribe_topics is None
 580        if topics is None:
 581            mock_logger.debug.assert_not_called()
 582        elif logging_enabled:
 583            mock_logger.debug.assert_called_once_with(msg="Unsubscribe topics")
 584        else:
 585            mock_logger.debug.assert_not_called()
 586        if expect_unsubscribe_call and logging_enabled:
 587            for topic in topics or []:
 588                mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(msg=f"Unsubscribed to {topic}")
 589        else:
 590            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()

 601    @pytest.mark.asyncio
 602    async def test_subscribe_command_exec(
 603        self,
 604        *,
 605        mocker: MockerFixture,
 606        mock_logger: MagicMock,
 607        manager: SyncComManager,
 608        topics: list[str],
 609        sub_results: list[int],
 610        expect_subscribe_call: bool,
 611        logging_enabled: bool,
 612    ) -> None:
 613        """Test that _subscribe_command_exec unsubscribes from prior topics,
 614        subscribes to the requested (non-empty) topics with the expected
 615        SubscribeOptions, logs success/failure per topic only when the relevant
 616        level is enabled, and always stores the new subscribe_params.
 617
 618        Args:
 619            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to build the mock
 620                client and patch _unsubscribe_topics.
 621            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
 622            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 623            topics (list[str]): The topics to subscribe to.
 624            sub_results (list[int]): The per-topic SUBACK results returned by the
 625                mock client.
 626            expect_subscribe_call (bool): Whether client.subscribe is expected to be
 627                awaited.
 628            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports every level as
 629                enabled.
 630
 631        Returns:
 632            None
 633        """
 634        # Arrange
 635        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
 636        client = mocker.MagicMock()
 637        client.subscribe = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=sub_results)
 638        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
 639        mock_unsubscribe = mocker.patch.object(
 640            SyncComManager, "_unsubscribe_topics", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
 641        )
 642        subscribe_params = SyncComManager.SubscribeCommand(
 643            topics=topics, max_qos=MqttQoS.QOS_1
 644        )
 645        # Act
 646        await manager._subscribe_command_exec(
 647            client=client, subscribe_params=subscribe_params
 648        )
 649        # Assert
 650        mock_unsubscribe.assert_awaited_once_with(client=client)
 651        if logging_enabled:
 652            mock_logger.debug.assert_called_once_with(
 653                msg=f"Command received: subscribe {subscribe_params}"
 654            )
 655        else:
 656            mock_logger.debug.assert_not_called()
 657        if expect_subscribe_call:
 658            client.subscribe.assert_awaited_once()
 659            sub_topic_list = client.subscribe.await_args.kwargs["topic"]
 660            assert [topic for topic, _ in sub_topic_list] == topics
 661            for _, options in sub_topic_list:
 662                assert options.QoS == MqttQoS.QOS_1
 663                assert options.noLocal is False
 664                assert options.retainAsPublished is False
 665                assert options.retainHandling == SubscribeOptions.RETAIN_DO_NOT_SEND
 666            if logging_enabled:
 667                for topic, result in zip(topics, sub_results, strict=True):
 668                    if result == MqttQoS.QOS_1:
 669                        mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
 670                            msg=f"Subscribed to {topic}: QoS {int(result)}"
 671                        )
 672                    else:
 673                        mock_logger.error.assert_any_call(
 674                            msg=f"Subscription to {topic} refused: "
 675                            f"{hex(result)} ({result:#04x})"
 676                        )
 677            else:
 678                mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()
 679                mock_logger.warning.assert_not_called()
 680                mock_logger.error.assert_not_called()
 681        else:
 682            client.subscribe.assert_not_awaited()
 683        assert manager._subscribe_topics == subscribe_params

 832    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
 833        argnames="scenario",
 834        argvalues=["initial_subscribe", "subscribe_command", "invalid_command"],
 835    )
 836    @pytest.mark.asyncio
 837    async def test_incoming_command_thread(
 838        self,
 839        mocker: MockerFixture,
 840        mock_logger: MagicMock,
 841        manager: SyncComManager,
 842        scenario: str,
 843    ) -> None:
 844        """Test that _incoming_command_thread performs an initial subscribe when
 845        _subscribe_topics is already set, dispatches SubscribeCommand items to
 846        their handler, logs a warning for any unrecognized item, and stops after
 847        handling an ExitThreadsCommand.
 848
 849        Args:
 850            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch the command
 851                handlers.
 852            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
 853            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
 854            scenario (str): Which command sequence to exercise.
 855
 856        Returns:
 857            None
 858        """
 859        # Arrange
 860        client = mocker.MagicMock()
 861        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why these are class-level patches.
 862        mock_subscribe_exec = mocker.patch.object(
 863            SyncComManager, "_subscribe_command_exec", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
 864        )
 865        mock_exit_threads = mocker.patch.object(
 866            SyncComManager, "_exit_threads", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
 867        )
 868        subscribe_command = SyncComManager.SubscribeCommand(
 869            topics=["topic_1"], max_qos=MqttQoS.QOS_1
 870        )
 871        incoming_queue: asyncio.Queue[SyncComManager.Command] = asyncio.Queue()
 872        manager._subscribe_topics = None
 873        if scenario == "initial_subscribe":
 874            manager._subscribe_topics = subscribe_command
 875            await incoming_queue.put(item=SyncComManager.ExitThreadsCommand())
 876        elif scenario == "subscribe_command":
 877            await incoming_queue.put(item=subscribe_command)
 878            await incoming_queue.put(item=SyncComManager.ExitThreadsCommand())
 879        else:
 880            await incoming_queue.put(item="not_a_command")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
 881            await incoming_queue.put(item=SyncComManager.ExitThreadsCommand())
 882        # Act
 883        await manager._incoming_command_thread(
 884            client=client, incoming_queue=incoming_queue
 885        )
 886        # Assert
 887        if scenario in ("initial_subscribe", "subscribe_command"):
 888            mock_subscribe_exec.assert_awaited_once_with(
 889                client=client, subscribe_params=subscribe_command
 890            )
 891        else:
 892            mock_subscribe_exec.assert_not_awaited()
 893            mock_logger.warning.assert_called_once()
 894        mock_exit_threads.assert_awaited_once_with()

 952
 953        Returns:
 954            None
 955        """

 958        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
 959        mock_client = mocker.MagicMock()
 960        async_cm = mocker.MagicMock()
 961        async_cm.__aenter__ = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=mock_client)
 962        async_cm.__aexit__ = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=False)
 963        mock_async_com_manager_class = mocker.patch(
 964            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.AsyncComManager", return_value=async_cm
 965        )
 966        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why these are class-level patches.
 967        mocker.patch.object(
 968            SyncComManager, "_message_receive_thread", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
 969        )
 970        mocker.patch.object(
 971            SyncComManager, "_incoming_command_thread", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
 972        )

 974        await manager._async_run(incoming_queue=asyncio.Queue())

 984            )

 986        else:
 987            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()

1035    @pytest.mark.parametrize(argnames="logging_enabled", argvalues=[True, False])
1036    @pytest.mark.asyncio
1037    async def test_async_run_retry_then_success(
1038        self,
1039        mocker: MockerFixture,
1040        mock_logger: MagicMock,
1041        manager: SyncComManager,
1042        logging_enabled: bool,
1043    ) -> None:
1044        """Test that _async_run retries after a connection failure: it logs the
1045        exception, transitions to RECONNECTING, sleeps for reconnect_interval, and
1046        then succeeds on the next attempt, only logging when the relevant level is
1047        enabled.
1048
1049        Args:
1050            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to mock the
1051                AsyncComManager collaborator, the background threads, and
1052                asyncio_sleep.
1053            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
1054            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1055            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports every level as
1056                enabled.
1057
1058        Returns:
1059            None
1060        """
1061        # Arrange
1062        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1063        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
1064        mock_client = mocker.MagicMock()
1065        bad_cm = mocker.MagicMock()
1066        bad_cm.__aenter__ = mocker.AsyncMock(side_effect=Exception("connect failed"))
1067        bad_cm.__aexit__ = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=False)
1068        good_cm = mocker.MagicMock()
1069        good_cm.__aenter__ = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=mock_client)
1070        good_cm.__aexit__ = mocker.AsyncMock(return_value=False)
1071        mock_async_com_manager_class = mocker.patch(
1072            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.AsyncComManager", side_effect=[bad_cm, good_cm]
1073        )
1074        mock_sleep = mocker.patch(
1075            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.asyncio_sleep", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
1076        )
1077        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why these are class-level patches.
1078        mocker.patch.object(
1079            SyncComManager, "_message_receive_thread", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
1080        )
1081        mocker.patch.object(
1082            SyncComManager, "_incoming_command_thread", new=mocker.AsyncMock()
1083        )
1084        # Act
1085        await manager._async_run(incoming_queue=asyncio.Queue())
1086        # Assert
1087        assert mock_async_com_manager_class.call_count == 2
1088        mock_sleep.assert_awaited_once_with(delay=manager._params.reconnect_interval)
1089        if logging_enabled:
1090            mock_logger.exception.assert_called_once_with(msg="Exception happened")
1091            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
1092                msg="All threads stopped and connection dropped"
1093            )
1094            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
1095                msg=f"Connection retry after {manager._params.reconnect_interval}"
1096            )
1097            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
1098                msg=f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.RECONNECTING.name}"
1099            )
1100            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
1101                msg=f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.CONNECTED.name}"
1102            )
1103        else:
1104            mock_logger.exception.assert_not_called()
1105            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()
1106        assert manager.connection_status == ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED

1108    @pytest.mark.parametrize(argnames="logging_enabled", argvalues=[True, False])
1109    def test_run(
1110        self,
1111        *,
1112        mocker: MockerFixture,
1113        mock_logger: MagicMock,
1114        manager: SyncComManager,
1115        logging_enabled: bool,
1116    ) -> None:
1117        """Test that _run runs _async_run() inside a Runner, logging its start/end
1118        messages only when INFO is enabled. Since the Runner does not raise here,
1119        this exercises the single-attempt path of the retry loop: one Runner is
1120        created, run once, and the loop exits without retrying and without
1121        disabling the thread.
1122
1123        Args:
1124            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch Runner
1125                and _async_run.
1126            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
1127            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1128            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports INFO as enabled.
1129
1130        Returns:
1131            None
1132        """
1133        # Arrange
1134        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1135        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
1136        mock_coro = mocker.MagicMock()
1137        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
1138        mocker.patch.object(
1139            SyncComManager, "_async_run", new=mocker.MagicMock(return_value=mock_coro)
1140        )
1141        mock_runner_instance = mocker.MagicMock()
1142        mock_runner_instance.__enter__.return_value = mock_runner_instance
1143        mock_runner_instance.__exit__.return_value = False
1144        mock_runner_class = mocker.patch(
1145            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.Runner", return_value=mock_runner_instance
1146        )
1147        mock_sleep = mocker.patch("step_lib.sync_com_manager.time_sleep")
1148        # Act
1149        manager._run()
1150        # Assert
1151        mock_runner_class.assert_called_once()
1152        mock_runner_instance.run.assert_called_once_with(coro=mock_coro)
1153        mock_sleep.assert_not_called()
1154        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STARTED
1155        assert manager._async_loop is None
1156        assert manager.connection_status == ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED
1157        if logging_enabled:
1158            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(msg="Thread async start execution")
1159            mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(msg="Thread async execution end")
1160        else:
1161            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()

1187    @pytest.mark.parametrize(argnames="logging_enabled", argvalues=[True, False])
1188    def test_run_survives_unhandled_exceptions_and_keeps_retrying(
1189        self,
1190        mocker: MockerFixture,
1191        mock_logger: MagicMock,
1192        manager: SyncComManager,
1193        logging_enabled: bool,
1194    ) -> None:
1195        """Test that _run does not stop the background thread when a BaseException
1196        escapes the Runner (e.g. a CancelledError/BaseExceptionGroup surfaced by the
1197        TaskGroup, which _async_run's own internal ``except BaseException`` retry loop
1198        would not catch). Instead, _run must log the failure (when enabled), sleep
1199        for reconnect_interval, and rebuild the event loop from scratch, over and
1200        over, with no cap on the number of attempts, as long as the manager stays
1201        enabled.
1202
1203        Args:
1204            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch _async_run,
1205                Runner, and time_sleep.
1206            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
1207            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1208            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports every level as
1209                enabled.
1210
1211        Returns:
1212            None
1213        """
1214
1215        class _EscapesExceptionCatch(BaseException):
1216            """A BaseException that is not an Exception, like CancelledError."""
1217
1218        # Arrange
1219        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1220        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
1221        failure_count = 5
1222        mock_coro = mocker.MagicMock()
1223        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
1224        mocker.patch.object(
1225            SyncComManager, "_async_run", new=mocker.MagicMock(return_value=mock_coro)
1226        )
1227
1228        def make_runner_instance(*, fails: bool) -> MagicMock:
1229            """Build a mocked Runner context manager that either raises or succeeds.
1230
1231            Args:
1232                fails (bool): Whether runner.run() should raise
1233                    _EscapesExceptionCatch instead of returning normally.
1234
1235            Returns:
1236                MagicMock: The mocked Runner instance.
1237
1238            Complexity:
1239                - Time: O(1), builds a fixed, constant number of mock attributes.
1240                - Space: O(1), only a fixed, small number of local objects/references
1241                  is created.
1242            """
1243            instance = cast("MagicMock", mocker.MagicMock())
1244            instance.__enter__.return_value = instance
1245            instance.__exit__.return_value = False
1246            if fails:
1247                instance.run.side_effect = _EscapesExceptionCatch("escaped")
1248            return instance
1249
1250        runner_instances = [
1251            make_runner_instance(fails=True) for _ in range(failure_count)
1252        ]
1253        runner_instances.append(make_runner_instance(fails=False))
1254        mock_runner_class = mocker.patch(
1255            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.Runner", side_effect=runner_instances
1256        )
1257        mock_sleep = mocker.patch("step_lib.sync_com_manager.time_sleep")
1258        # Act
1259        manager._run()
1260        # Assert: the thread survived every failure and rebuilt the loop each time,
1261        # rather than letting the exception propagate out of _run.
1262        assert mock_runner_class.call_count == failure_count + 1
1263        assert mock_sleep.call_count == failure_count
1264        mock_sleep.assert_called_with(manager._params.reconnect_interval)
1265        # The manager was never told to stop, so it remains enabled and only the
1266        # final, successful attempt's cleanup ran.
1267        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STARTED
1268        assert manager._async_loop is None
1269        assert manager.connection_status == ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED
1270        if not logging_enabled:
1271            mock_logger.exception.assert_not_called()
1272            mock_logger.info.assert_not_called()
1273            return
1274        assert mock_logger.exception.call_count == failure_count
1275        mock_logger.exception.assert_called_with(
1276            msg="Unhandled exception escaped the async event loop"
1277        )
1278        mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(msg="Thread async execution end")
1279        # Each failed attempt must republish DISCONNECTED immediately, then
1280        # RECONNECTING once the retry delay has elapsed, so other threads never
1281        # observe a stale "connected" status while the loop is being rebuilt; the
1282        # final, successful attempt's cleanup then republishes DISCONNECTED once more.
1283        status_log_calls = [
1284            call.kwargs.get("msg", "")
1285            for call in mock_logger.info.call_args_list
1286            if call.kwargs.get("msg", "").startswith("Connection status: ")
1287        ]
1288        assert (
1289            status_log_calls.count(
1290                f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED.name}"
1291            )
1292            == failure_count + 1
1293        )
1294        assert (
1295            status_log_calls.count(
1296                f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.RECONNECTING.name}"
1297            )
1298            == failure_count
1299        )

1301    def test_run_creates_a_fresh_incoming_queue_per_event_loop(
1302        self, mocker: MockerFixture, manager: SyncComManager
1303    ) -> None:
1304        """Test that every event loop _run builds gets its own incoming command queue.
1305
1306        An asyncio.Queue binds to the first loop that waits on it, so reusing the
1307        queue of a crashed loop on the rebuilt one would fail. The Runner fails once
1308        and then succeeds: each attempt must hand _async_run a new queue, sized from
1309        max_incoming_queue_rooms, and publish it together with its loop.
1310
1311        Args:
1312            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch Runner,
1313                _async_run, and time_sleep.
1314            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1315
1316        Returns:
1317            None
1318        """
1319        # Arrange
1320        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1321        seen: list[tuple[object, object]] = []
1322
1323        def fake_async_run(
1324            _self: SyncComManager, incoming_queue: asyncio.Queue[SyncComManager.Command]
1325        ) -> MagicMock:
1326            """Record the given queue and the one published on the manager.
1327
1328            Args:
1329                _self (SyncComManager): The manager the method is bound to.
1330                incoming_queue (asyncio.Queue[SyncComManager.Command]): The queue
1331                    handed to _async_run.
1332
1333            Returns:
1334                MagicMock: A stand-in for the coroutine object.
1335            """
1336            seen.append((incoming_queue, manager._incoming_queue))
1337            return cast("MagicMock", mocker.MagicMock())
1338
1339        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
1340        mocker.patch.object(SyncComManager, "_async_run", new=fake_async_run)
1341        failing_runner = mocker.MagicMock()
1342        failing_runner.__enter__.return_value = failing_runner
1343        failing_runner.__exit__.return_value = False
1344        failing_runner.run.side_effect = RuntimeError("loop crashed")
1345        good_runner = mocker.MagicMock()
1346        good_runner.__enter__.return_value = good_runner
1347        good_runner.__exit__.return_value = False
1348        mocker.patch(
1349            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.Runner",
1350            side_effect=[failing_runner, good_runner],
1351        )
1352        mocker.patch("step_lib.sync_com_manager.time_sleep")
1353        # Act
1354        manager._run()
1355        # Assert
1356        assert len(seen) == 2
1357        (first_given, first_published), (second_given, second_published) = seen
1358        assert first_given is first_published
1359        assert second_given is second_published
1360        assert first_given is not second_given
1361        for queue in (first_given, second_given):
1362            assert isinstance(queue, asyncio.Queue)
1363            assert queue.maxsize == manager._params.max_incoming_queue_rooms
1364        # Once _run ends, neither the loop nor its queue stays published
1365        assert manager._async_loop is None
1366        assert manager._incoming_queue is None

1407    def test_run_republishes_disconnected_state_before_retrying(
1408        self, mocker: MockerFixture, manager: SyncComManager
1409    ) -> None:
1410        """Test that, during the backoff between a failed attempt and the
1411        next Runner being constructed, ``_async_loop`` has already been reset
1412        to ``None`` and the connection status has already moved to
1413        RECONNECTING -- not left pointing at the event loop that just
1414        crashed. This is what lets start()/stop()/subscribe()/
1415        publish_its_message()/get_its_message_received(), called from
1416        another thread during the retry window, correctly see "loop not
1417        running" instead of trying to schedule work on an already-closed
1418        event loop. ``_async_loop`` is reassigned to the new, non-None loop
1419        as soon as the retried Runner is entered, before its ``run()`` is
1420        invoked, so that reassignment -- not ``run()`` -- is where the
1421        retry window ends and must be observed from.
1422
1423        Args:
1424            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch _async_run,
1425                Runner, and time_sleep.
1426            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1427
1428        Returns:
1429            None
1430        """
1431
1432        class _EscapesExceptionCatch(BaseException):
1433            """A BaseException that is not an Exception, like CancelledError."""
1434
1435        # Arrange
1436        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1437        mock_coro = mocker.MagicMock()
1438        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
1439        mocker.patch.object(
1440            SyncComManager, "_async_run", new=mocker.MagicMock(return_value=mock_coro)
1441        )
1442        observed_state: dict[str, object] = {}
1443
1444        def failing_run(**_kwargs: MagicMock) -> None:
1445            """Simulate the first attempt crashing with an unhandled exception.
1446
1447            Args:
1448                **_kwargs (MagicMock): The keyword arguments passed to runner.run
1449                    (ignored; present only to match the real call signature).
1450
1451            Returns:
1452                None
1453            """
1454            raise _EscapesExceptionCatch("escaped")
1455
1456        failing_instance = cast("MagicMock", mocker.MagicMock())
1457        failing_instance.__enter__.return_value = failing_instance
1458        failing_instance.__exit__.return_value = False
1459        failing_instance.run.side_effect = failing_run
1460        succeeding_instance = cast("MagicMock", mocker.MagicMock())
1461        succeeding_instance.__enter__.return_value = succeeding_instance
1462        succeeding_instance.__exit__.return_value = False
1463
1464        runner_instances = iter([failing_instance, succeeding_instance])
1465
1466        def next_runner_instance(**_kwargs: MagicMock) -> MagicMock:
1467            """Hand back the next scripted Runner instance, recording manager
1468            state right before the retried (second) Runner is constructed.
1469
1470            Args:
1471                **_kwargs (MagicMock): The keyword arguments passed to
1472                    Runner() (ignored; present only to match the real call
1473                    signature).
1474
1475            Returns:
1476                MagicMock: The next scripted Runner instance.
1477            """
1478            instance = next(runner_instances)
1479            if instance is succeeding_instance:
1480                observed_state["async_loop"] = manager._async_loop
1481                observed_state["connection_status"] = manager.connection_status
1482            return instance
1483
1484        mocker.patch(
1485            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.Runner", side_effect=next_runner_instance
1486        )
1487        mocker.patch("step_lib.sync_com_manager.time_sleep")
1488        # Act
1489        manager._run()
1490        # Assert
1491        assert observed_state["async_loop"] is None
1492        assert observed_state["connection_status"] == ConnectionStatus.RECONNECTING

1494    def test_run_stops_retrying_once_stop_is_requested_mid_failure(
1495        self, mocker: MockerFixture, mock_logger: MagicMock, manager: SyncComManager
1496    ) -> None:
1497        """Test that _run gives up retrying, without sleeping or rebuilding the loop
1498        again, once ``_system_status`` moves out of STARTING/STARTED (e.g. because
1499        ``stop()`` was called from another thread) while a Runner attempt is failing.
1500
1501        Args:
1502            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch _async_run,
1503                Runner, and time_sleep.
1504            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
1505            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
1506
1507        Returns:
1508            None
1509        """
1510        # Arrange
1511        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
1512        mock_coro = mocker.MagicMock()
1513        # See TestSyncComManager.test_enter for why this is a class-level patch.
1514        mocker.patch.object(
1515            SyncComManager, "_async_run", new=mocker.MagicMock(return_value=mock_coro)
1516        )
1517
1518        def fail_and_disable(**_kwargs: MagicMock) -> None:
1519            """Simulate stop() disabling the thread while the runner is failing.
1520
1521            Args:
1522                **_kwargs (MagicMock): The keyword arguments passed to runner.run
1523                    (ignored; present only to match the real call signature).
1524
1525            Returns:
1526                None
1527
1528            Complexity:
1529                - Time: O(1), a fixed, constant number of operations is performed.
1530                - Space: O(1), no additional storage is used.
1531            """
1532            manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STOPPING
1533            msg = "connection lost"
1534            raise RuntimeError(msg)
1535
1536        runner_instance = mocker.MagicMock()
1537        runner_instance.__enter__.return_value = runner_instance
1538        runner_instance.__exit__.return_value = False
1539        runner_instance.run.side_effect = fail_and_disable
1540        mock_runner_class = mocker.patch(
1541            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.Runner", return_value=runner_instance
1542        )
1543        mock_sleep = mocker.patch("step_lib.sync_com_manager.time_sleep")
1544        # Act
1545        manager._run()
1546        # Assert: the failure is logged, but there is no retry once disabled.
1547        assert mock_runner_class.call_count == 1
1548        mock_sleep.assert_not_called()
1549        mock_logger.exception.assert_called_once_with(
1550            msg="Unhandled exception escaped the async event loop"
1551        )
1552        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STOPPING
1553        assert manager._async_loop is None
1554        assert manager.connection_status == ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED
1555        # Giving up (rather than retrying) means RECONNECTING is never published;
1556        # only the immediate DISCONNECTED from the except block and the one from
1557        # the outer finally are logged.
1558        mock_logger.info.assert_any_call(
1559            msg=f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.DISCONNECTED.name}"
1560        )
1561        reconnecting_calls = [
1562            call
1563            for call in mock_logger.info.call_args_list
1564            if call.kwargs.get("msg")
1565            == f"Connection status: {ConnectionStatus.RECONNECTING.name}"
1566        ]
1567        assert reconnecting_calls == []

1789    def test_health_check_loop_calls_check_health_periodically(
1790        self,
1791        mocker: MockerFixture,
1792        sync_com_manager_params: SyncComManagerParams,
1793        mock_logger: MagicMock,
1794    ) -> None:
1795        """Test that _health_check_loop calls the pool's check_health(auto_restart=True)
1796        at least twice within a bounded wait, using a real thread and a small
1797        publish_health_check_interval, and stops promptly once
1798        the stop event it was given is set.
1799
1800        Args:
1801            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to build a mock
1802                pool.
1803            sync_com_manager_params (SyncComManagerParams): The base parameters,
1804                overridden here with a small publish_health_check_interval.
1805            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger to attach to the manager.
1806
1807        Returns:
1808            None
1809        """
1810        # Arrange
1811        manager = SyncComManager(
1812            params=replace(sync_com_manager_params, publish_health_check_interval=0.02),
1813            logger=mock_logger,
1814        )
1815        mock_pool = mocker.MagicMock()
1816        manager._worker_pool = mock_pool
1817        thread = Thread(
1818            target=manager._health_check_loop,
1819            kwargs={"stop_event": manager._health_check_stop_event},
1820            daemon=True,
1821        )
1822        # Act
1823        thread.start()
1824        deadline = time.monotonic() + 2.0
1825        while mock_pool.check_health.call_count < 2 and time.monotonic() < deadline:
1826            time.sleep(0.01)
1827        manager._health_check_stop_event.set()
1828        thread.join(timeout=2.0)
1829        # Assert
1830        assert not thread.is_alive()
1831        assert mock_pool.check_health.call_count >= 2
1832        mock_pool.check_health.assert_called_with(auto_restart=True)

2178    def test_start_serializes_concurrent_second_call(self) -> None:
2179        """Test that two threads calling start() concurrently on the same
2180        manager both succeed; the loser waits for the in-flight start and
2181        returns as a no-op instead of racing on the underlying Thread.start().
2182
2183        Unlike the fully-mocked tests above, this one deliberately runs
2184        real background threads (no mocking of Thread/_system_status),
2185        since the race being guarded against can only be observed with
2186        genuine concurrent execution. The target port is bound and
2187        immediately released so start() can proceed past the readiness
2188        wait without a real broker.
2189
2190        Returns:
2191            None
2192        """
2193        # Arrange
2194        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
2195            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
2196            unused_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
2197        params = SyncComManagerParams(
2198            instance_name="test_concurrent_start",
2199            host="127.0.0.1",
2200            port=unused_port,
2201            username="user",
2202            password="pass",
2203            reconnect_interval=1,
2204            timeout=15,
2205            max_incoming_queue_rooms=10,
2206            max_outgoing_queue_rooms=10,
2207            publish_worker_count=1,
2208        )
2209        manager = SyncComManager(
2210            params=params, logger=logging.getLogger("test_concurrent_start")
2211        )
2212        barrier = Barrier(2)
2213        results: list[StepLibError | None] = []
2214        results_lock = Lock()
2215
2216        def run_start() -> None:
2217            """Wait for both threads to be ready, then race start().
2218
2219            Returns:
2220                None
2221            """
2222            barrier.wait(timeout=5.0)
2223            try:
2224                manager.start()
2225            except StepLibError as error:
2226                with results_lock:
2227                    results.append(error)
2228            else:
2229                with results_lock:
2230                    results.append(None)
2231
2232        threads = [Thread(target=run_start) for _ in range(2)]
2233        try:
2234            # Act
2235            for thread in threads:
2236                thread.start()
2237            for thread in threads:
2238                thread.join(timeout=params.timeout)
2239                assert not thread.is_alive()
2240            # Assert
2241            assert results == [None, None]
2242            assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STARTED
2243        finally:
2244            manager.stop()

2269    @pytest.mark.parametrize(argnames="logging_enabled", argvalues=[True, False])
2270    def test_stop_success(
2271        self,
2272        mocker: MockerFixture,
2273        mock_logger: MagicMock,
2274        manager: SyncComManager,
2275        logging_enabled: bool,
2276    ) -> None:
2277        """Test that stop() disables the thread flag, schedules an ExitThreadsCommand
2278        on the async loop, joins the background thread, clears the loop reference,
2279        always closes the (here never-started, so effectively no-op) publish worker
2280        pool, and logs the stop command and the pool-closed message only when INFO
2281        is enabled.
2282
2283        Args:
2284            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to build a mock
2285                loop/thread and patch asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe.
2286            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager's params.
2287            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
2288            logging_enabled (bool): Whether the mock logger reports INFO as enabled.
2289
2290        Returns:
2291            None
2292        """
2293        # Arrange
2294        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
2295        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = logging_enabled
2296        mock_loop = mocker.MagicMock()
2297        manager._async_loop = mock_loop
2298        manager._incoming_queue = asyncio.Queue()
2299        mock_thread = mocker.MagicMock()
2300        mock_thread.is_alive.return_value = False
2301        manager._async_thread = mock_thread
2302        mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe = mocker.patch(
2303            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe"
2304        )
2305        # Act
2306        manager.stop()
2307        # Assert
2308        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STOPPED
2309        assert mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.call_count == 2
2310        put_call_kwargs, join_call_kwargs = (
2311            call.kwargs for call in mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.call_args_list
2312        )
2313        assert put_call_kwargs["loop"] is mock_loop
2314        assert asyncio.iscoroutine(put_call_kwargs["coro"])
2315        put_call_kwargs["coro"].close()
2316        assert join_call_kwargs["loop"] is mock_loop
2317        assert asyncio.iscoroutine(join_call_kwargs["coro"])
2318        join_call_kwargs["coro"].close()
2319        mock_thread.join.assert_called_once_with(timeout=manager._params.timeout)
2320        assert manager._async_loop is None
2321        result_calls = mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.return_value.result.call_args_list
2322        assert result_calls == [
2323            mocker.call(timeout=manager._params.timeout),
2324            mocker.call(timeout=manager._params.timeout),
2325        ]
2326        if logging_enabled:
2327            # The pool was never started, so close() is an idempotent no-op
2328            # and emits no "Publish worker pool closed" line.
2329            assert mock_logger.info.call_args_list == [
2330                mocker.call(msg="Command: thread async stop execution")
2331            ]

2342        This guards the defense-in-depth timeout added to stop()'s two blocking
2343        ``run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()`` calls: even if some
2344        unforeseen interleaving left them pending forever, stop() should fail
2345        loudly with a clear, typed error instead of hanging indefinitely.

2347        Args:

2361        manager._async_thread = mock_thread

2363            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe"
2364        )
2365        mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.return_value.result.side_effect = TimeoutError
2366        # Act & Assert
2367        with pytest.raises(StepLibError, match="Timed out"):
2368            manager.stop()
2369        # asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe is mocked, so the real
2370        # _incoming_queue.put(...) coroutine it was given is never awaited;
2371        # close it explicitly to avoid a "coroutine was never awaited" warning.
2372        mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.call_args.kwargs["coro"].close()

2436            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.

2438        Returns:
2439            None
2440        """
2441        # Arrange
2442        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
2443        manager._async_loop = mocker.MagicMock()
2444        manager._incoming_queue = asyncio.Queue()
2445        mock_thread = mocker.MagicMock()
2446        mock_thread.is_alive.return_value = True
2447        manager._async_thread = mock_thread
2448        mock_worker_pool = mocker.MagicMock()
2449        manager._worker_pool = mock_worker_pool
2450        mock_health_check_thread = mocker.MagicMock()
2451        # A non-None ident simulates a thread that was actually started, so
2452        # stop() must join it; is_alive() False simulates a clean join.
2453        mock_health_check_thread.ident = 123
2454        mock_health_check_thread.is_alive.return_value = False
2455        manager._health_check_thread = mock_health_check_thread
2456        mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe = mocker.patch(
2457            "step_lib.sync_com_manager.asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe",
2458            side_effect=RuntimeError("boom"),
2459        )
2460        # Act & Assert
2461        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="boom"):
2462            manager.stop()
2463        assert manager._health_check_stop_event.is_set() is True
2464        mock_health_check_thread.join.assert_called_once_with(
2465            timeout=manager._params.timeout
2466        )
2467        mock_worker_pool.close.assert_called_once_with()
2468        # asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe is mocked, so the real
2469        # _incoming_queue.put(...) coroutine it was given (built before the
2470        # mock's side_effect fires, since keyword arguments are evaluated
2471        # before the call) is never awaited; close it explicitly to avoid a
2472        # "coroutine was never awaited" warning.
2473        mock_run_coroutine_threadsafe.call_args.kwargs["coro"].close()

2475    def test_stop_serializes_concurrent_second_call(self) -> None:
2476        """Test that two threads calling stop() concurrently on a started
2477        manager both succeed; the loser waits for the in-flight stop and
2478        returns as a no-op instead of racing through duplicate teardown.
2479
2480        Unlike the fully-mocked tests above, this one deliberately runs
2481        real background threads, since the race being guarded against can
2482        only be observed with genuine concurrent execution.
2483
2484        Returns:
2485            None
2486        """
2487        # Arrange
2488        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
2489            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
2490            unused_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
2491        params = SyncComManagerParams(
2492            instance_name="test_concurrent_stop",
2493            host="127.0.0.1",
2494            port=unused_port,
2495            username="user",
2496            password="pass",
2497            reconnect_interval=1,
2498            timeout=15,
2499            max_incoming_queue_rooms=10,
2500            max_outgoing_queue_rooms=10,
2501            publish_worker_count=1,
2502        )
2503        manager = SyncComManager(
2504            params=params, logger=logging.getLogger("test_concurrent_stop")
2505        )
2506        manager.start()
2507        barrier = Barrier(2)
2508        results: list[StepLibError | None] = []
2509        results_lock = Lock()
2510
2511        def run_stop() -> None:
2512            """Wait for both threads to be ready, then race stop().
2513
2514            Returns:
2515                None
2516            """
2517            barrier.wait(timeout=5.0)
2518            try:
2519                manager.stop()
2520            except StepLibError as error:
2521                with results_lock:
2522                    results.append(error)
2523            else:
2524                with results_lock:
2525                    results.append(None)
2526
2527        threads = [Thread(target=run_stop) for _ in range(2)]
2528        # Act
2529        for thread in threads:
2530            thread.start()
2531        for thread in threads:
2532            thread.join(timeout=params.timeout)
2533            assert not thread.is_alive()
2534        # Assert
2535        assert results == [None, None]
2536        assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STOPPED

2538    def test_stop_during_reconnect_does_not_hang_or_raise_unexpectedly(self) -> None:
2539        """Test that stop() completes cleanly when called while the manager is
2540        disconnected/reconnecting, instead of hanging or raising an unexpected
2541        CancelledError.
2542
2543        Unlike every other test in this file, this one deliberately runs a real
2544        background Thread with a real asyncio event loop (no mocking of
2545        asyncio_run_coroutine_threadsafe or the thread), because the bug this
2546        guards against only manifests from a genuine race between the calling
2547        thread and the event-loop thread: _incoming_command_thread (the only
2548        code that ever calls _incoming_queue.task_done()) only exists while
2549        _async_run is inside a live connection, so calling stop() while
2550        disconnected previously left its _incoming_queue.join() pending forever
2551        or cancelled at loop teardown. The target port is bound and immediately
2552        released so the connection attempt is refused right away, reliably
2553        keeping the manager in the disconnected/reconnecting window for the
2554        whole test.
2555
2556        params.timeout is set well above reconnect_interval (rather than just
2557        above it) because on Windows the refused connection itself can
2558        occasionally take a few seconds to surface (observed up to ~4s under
2559        load) before _async_run even reaches its reconnect_interval sleep;
2560        without that headroom the test flakes on environment-dependent
2561        connect-refusal latency that has nothing to do with the drain logic
2562        under test.
2563
2564        Returns:
2565            None
2566        """
2567        # Arrange
2568        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
2569            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
2570            unused_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
2571        params = SyncComManagerParams(
2572            instance_name="test_stop_during_reconnect",
2573            host="127.0.0.1",
2574            port=unused_port,
2575            username="user",
2576            password="pass",
2577            reconnect_interval=1,
2578            timeout=15,
2579            max_incoming_queue_rooms=10,
2580            max_outgoing_queue_rooms=10,
2581            publish_worker_count=1,
2582        )
2583        manager = SyncComManager(
2584            params=params, logger=logging.getLogger("test_stop_during_reconnect")
2585        )
2586        manager.start()
2587        try:
2588            # No sleep needed: the connection attempt is refused essentially
2589            # instantly (nothing listens on unused_port), so the manager is
2590            # already disconnected/retrying by the time stop() below runs.
2591            start_time = time.monotonic()
2592            # Act
2593            manager.stop()
2594            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
2595        finally:
2596            # Best-effort cleanup should stop() itself have failed/timed out,
2597            # so this test never leaves a background thread running.
2598            if manager._async_thread.is_alive():
2599                manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STOPPING
2600                manager._async_thread.join(timeout=params.timeout)
2601        # Assert
2602        assert manager._async_loop is None
2603        assert not manager._async_thread.is_alive()
2604        # Comfortably under params.timeout: proves the primary fix (draining
2605        # _incoming_queue in _async_run before it returns) ran, rather than
2606        # stop() only succeeding via the defense-in-depth timeout fallback.
2607        assert elapsed < params.timeout

2609    def test_restart_after_stop(self) -> None:
2610        """Test that a manager can be started and stopped repeatedly.
2611
2612        Like test_stop_during_reconnect_does_not_hang_or_raise_unexpectedly, this
2613        runs a real background Thread, a real asyncio event loop, and a real publish
2614        worker pool against a refused port, since the failure it guards against
2615        (``threading.Thread.start`` called twice, and an asyncio.Queue reused on a
2616        second event loop) only shows up with the real primitives. Every start()
2617        must build new threads, and every stop() must complete well within
2618        params.timeout.
2619
2620        Returns:
2621            None
2622        """
2623        # Arrange
2624        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
2625            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
2626            unused_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
2627        params = SyncComManagerParams(
2628            instance_name="test_restart_after_stop",
2629            host="127.0.0.1",
2630            port=unused_port,
2631            username="user",
2632            password="pass",
2633            reconnect_interval=1,
2634            timeout=15,
2635            max_incoming_queue_rooms=10,
2636            max_outgoing_queue_rooms=10,
2637            publish_worker_count=1,
2638        )
2639        manager = SyncComManager(
2640            params=params, logger=logging.getLogger("test_restart_after_stop")
2641        )
2642        async_threads: list[Thread] = []
2643        health_check_threads: list[Thread] = []
2644        try:
2645            for _ in range(2):
2646                # Act
2647                manager.start()
2648                async_threads.append(manager._async_thread)
2649                health_check_threads.append(manager._health_check_thread)
2650                assert manager._worker_pool.is_running is True
2651                start_time = time.monotonic()
2652                manager.stop()
2653                elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
2654                # Assert
2655                assert elapsed < params.timeout
2656                assert manager._system_status == _SystemStatus.STOPPED
2657                assert manager._async_loop is None
2658                assert manager._incoming_queue is None
2659                assert manager._worker_pool.is_running is False
2660        finally:
2661            # Best-effort cleanup should an iteration have failed midway, so this
2662            # test never leaves a background thread or worker process running.
2663            if manager._async_thread.is_alive():
2664                manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STOPPING
2665                manager._health_check_stop_event.set()
2666                manager._async_thread.join(timeout=params.timeout)
2667            manager._worker_pool.close()
2668        assert async_threads[0] is not async_threads[1]
2669        assert health_check_threads[0] is not health_check_threads[1]
2670        for thread in (*async_threads, *health_check_threads):
2671            assert not thread.is_alive()

3024            PublishEnvelope, "from_domain_objects"

3162    def test_publish_its_message_does_not_block_and_raises_when_workers_saturated(
3163        self,
3164    ) -> None:
3165        """Test that publish_its_message(), sent to a real publish worker process
3166        pool, returns promptly by raising StepLibBackpressureError instead of
3167        blocking once every worker's send pipe has reached its high-water mark.
3168
3169        Unlike the fully-mocked tests above, this one deliberately spawns real
3170        publish worker processes (a tiny publish_worker_count/publish_hwm) against
3171        an unreachable MQTT port: proving the call does not block can only be
3172        observed against genuine ZMQ sockets and OS processes, since a mocked pool
3173        can't distinguish "returned immediately" from "would have waited forever."
3174        Because nothing ever connects to MQTT, the workers never drain their PULL
3175        sockets, so the PUSH socket's pipes fill up quickly.
3176
3177        Returns:
3178            None
3179        """
3180        # Arrange
3181        with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as probe:
3182            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
3183            unused_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
3184        params = SyncComManagerParams(
3185            instance_name="test_publish_backpressure",
3186            host="127.0.0.1",
3187            port=unused_port,
3188            username="user",
3189            password="pass",
3190            reconnect_interval=5,
3191            timeout=15,
3192            max_incoming_queue_rooms=2,
3193            max_outgoing_queue_rooms=2,
3194            publish_worker_count=1,
3195            publish_hwm=1,
3196            publish_max_connect_attempts=1000,
3197        )
3198        manager = SyncComManager(
3199            params=params, logger=logging.getLogger("test_publish_backpressure")
3200        )
3201        manager.start()
3202        try:
3203            # A real, supported FacilityMessage is required here: unlike the
3204            # mocked-boundary unit tests above, this test exercises the real
3205            # PublishEnvelope.from_domain_objects()/JSON encoding end-to-end, and
3206            # a mock would fail its `case CamMessageV1(): ...` match before ever
3207            # reaching the pool.
3208            message = CamMessageV1(message_param=CamDataV1.get_default())
3209            address = GeoNetworkAddress(
3210                traffic_participant_type=TrafficParticipantType.PASSENGER_CAR, mac_id=1
3211            )
3212            position = GpsLocation(
3213                time=message.its_time,
3214                latitude=1.0,
3215                longitude=2.0,
3216                accuracy=None,
3217                speed=None,
3218                heading=None,
3219            )
3220            # Act: publish until backpressure is observed, bounded so a
3221            # regression (backpressure never triggering) fails fast rather than
3222            # hanging.
3223            start_time = time.monotonic()
3224            backpressure_hit = False
3225            for _ in range(2000):
3226                try:
3227                    manager.publish_its_message(
3228                        message=message, address=address, current_position=position
3229                    )
3230                except StepLibBackpressureError:
3231                    backpressure_hit = True
3232                    break
3233            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
3234            # Assert: backpressure was observed, and every publish attempt
3235            # (including the final, backpressure-raising one) returned promptly
3236            # rather than blocking.
3237            assert backpressure_hit
3238            assert elapsed < 5.0
3239        finally:
3240            manager.stop()

3366    def test_two_signals_stop_once(
3367        self, mocker: MockerFixture, manager: SyncComManager
3368    ) -> None:
3369        """Test that two signals, each handled on its own thread, run the teardown
3370        only once.
3371
3372        Args:
3373            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture used to patch _stop().
3374            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
3375
3376        Returns:
3377            None
3378        """
3379
3380        # Arrange
3381        def fake_stop() -> None:
3382            """Take a little time, then settle as the real _stop() does."""
3383            time.sleep(0.1)
3384            with manager._cond:
3385                manager._set_status(new_status=_SystemStatus.STOPPED)
3386                manager._cond.notify_all()
3387
3388        teardown = mocker.patch.object(SyncComManager, "_stop", side_effect=fake_stop)
3389        manager._system_status = _SystemStatus.STARTED
3390        threads = [threading.Thread(target=manager._stop_from_signal) for _ in range(2)]
3391        # Act
3392        for thread in threads:
3393            thread.start()
3394        for thread in threads:
3395            thread.join(timeout=10.0)
3396        # Assert
3397        teardown.assert_called_once_with()
3398        assert manager._system_status is _SystemStatus.STOPPED

3575    def test_settle_budget_formula(self, manager: SyncComManager) -> None:

3577        and four bounded manager waits.

3580            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.

3586        params = manager._params
3587        attempt = (
3588            PublishWorkerPool.SPAWN_OVERHEAD
3589            + params.publish_worker_startup_timeout
3590            + 2 * params.publish_forceful_join_timeout
3591        )
3592        expected = (
3593            params.publish_worker_count
3594            * PublishWorkerPool.MAX_WORKER_SPAWN_ATTEMPTS
3595            * attempt
3596            + attempt
3597            + 2 * params.publish_graceful_shutdown_timeout
3598            + params.publish_worker_count * 2 * params.publish_forceful_join_timeout
3599            + 4 * params.timeout
3600            + PublishWorkerPool.TIMEOUT_MARGIN
3601        )
3602        # Act & Assert
3603        assert manager._settle_budget() == pytest.approx(expected)

3728    async def test_incoming_command_thread_invalid_command_silent_when_disabled(
3729        self, mocker: MockerFixture, mock_logger: MagicMock, manager: SyncComManager
3730    ) -> None:
3731        """Test an invalid command is skipped without a WARNING when that level is
3732        disabled, and the queue still marks it done.
3733
3734        Args:
3735            mocker (MockerFixture): The pytest-mock fixture.
3736            mock_logger (MagicMock): The mock Logger attached to the manager.
3737            manager (SyncComManager): The manager instance under test.
3738
3739        Returns:
3740            None
3741        """
3742        # Arrange
3743        mock_logger.isEnabledFor.return_value = False
3744        mocker.patch.object(SyncComManager, "_exit_threads", new=mocker.AsyncMock())
3745        incoming_queue: asyncio.Queue[Any] = asyncio.Queue()
3746        incoming_queue.put_nowait("not a command")
3747        incoming_queue.put_nowait(SyncComManager.ExitThreadsCommand())
3748        # Act
3749        await manager._incoming_command_thread(
3750            client=mocker.MagicMock(), incoming_queue=incoming_queue
3751        )
3752        # Assert
3753        mock_logger.warning.assert_not_called()
3754        await asyncio.wait_for(incoming_queue.join(), timeout=1.0)
